audit.note: toggle is wired roundtrip-free via follow_up_action( control_global, MESSAGE_TOAST.show )

deviations.what: onToggle vetoes the firing when the matching Switch is on (event.preventDefault) and resets that Switch. **Reproduced 1:1 since 2026-08-23** with s_ctrl-prevent_default_expr: the client expression (!${$parameters>/expanded} && {/PREVENT_COLLAPSE}) || (${$parameters>/expanded} && {/PREVENT_EXPAND}) is evaluated when the event fires and reads the two two-way bound Switch states, which is exactly what the original handler does. The event still reaches the backend either way, and on_event raises the matching toast and resets that Switch. Two defects of the earlier shape are gone with it. (1) The boolean s_ctrl-check_prevent_default is baked into the XML at RENDER time and the Switches carry no event, so a flipped Switch only reached the wire on the next render: the first toggle after a flip - the one the flip was meant to block - was never vetoed. The sidecar's claim that the direction of the next toggle is known and the round-trip re-bakes the flag was wrong on both halves. (2) The TOGGLE branch ended in view_display( ), and a re-render hands back a fresh control tree: SidePanel.selectedItem is an association and sideContentExpanded a hidden property, so the side content the user had just opened collapsed again on every toggle - the sample's central interaction never persisted. There is no re-render any more; the Switch reset travels with the automatic model push.

the SidePanel and SidePanelItem controls (both since UI5 1.107) are newer than 1.71 but are the whole point of this sample and kept for the 1:1 port - the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.107 to render it. @since verified in sap/f/SidePanel.js and sap/f/SidePanelItem.js:34 (control-level, which the member-level property gate never saw).
